newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SABENA CONFIRMS TALKS WITH SAFRICAN CARRIER.
newsitem.headline: SABENA CONFIRMS TALKS WITH SAFRICAN CARRIER.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena on Thursday confirmed a newspaper report it might link up with South African domestic airline Nationwide Air.
"We are having talks with Nationwide," Sabena spokesman Erik Sclep told Reuters.
"But it's really just the first stage... We're just trying to establish how closely we can cooperate and what it could mean for Nationwide in Europe and for us in South Africa," he said.
South Africa's Business Day newspaper, citing unnamed industry sources, earlier said that details of the deal were expected to be announced later this week.
If Sabena, 49.5 percent owned by Swissair decides to go ahead with the deal, it will do so this year, Sclep said.
"We still have to see what's possible, whether for instance it could be a code-share deal, a real partnership or joint flight numbers," he said.
Nationwide has 11 BAC 1-11 aircraft, two Boeing 727s and five King Air aircraft on flights from Johannesburg to Cape Town, George and Port Elizabeth.
